financing.summary: DRB Group is not a stand-alone borrower: it is a 92.48%-owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry (via Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc.), files nothing with the SEC, has no rated debt, and publishes no lot counts, credit lines or lenders of its own. Trade press says Sumitomo funds DRB by keeping earnings in the business and adding shareholder loans; the parent in turn carried JPY 1,659.7 billion of interest-bearing debt at 30 September 2026 after buying Tri Pointe Homes with a JPY 835.1 billion SMBC bridge loan, about JPY 260 billion of which still has to be moved to permanent financing. The Brightland Homes piece folded into DRB in April 2025 (now DRB Group Texas, LLC) was lightly levered: USD 1,470.4M of total assets against USD 870.8M of net assets at December 2024. Land: Sumitomo says its U.S. builders should use option contracts to cut the financial burden of land, yet the five pre-Tri Pointe builders, of which DRB is by far the largest, cut optioned lots 23.7% in the year to September 2026 (to 23,500 of 73,971, about 32%) while owned lots held flat at about 50,500. For a land banker that is the opening: a stated parent policy in favour of options, a falling option ratio, a parent focused on deleveraging and protecting its rating, and no named land banker or lot-option financier anywhere in the public record.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning owned, with a parent-stated push toward options. DRB historically develops its own land: its releases say it 'develops land for its two builders' (DRB Homes, DRB Elevate 55+) and its DRB Group Development arm does fee-based entitlement, land development and build-to-rent work for investors. Under Sumitomo Forestry's U.S. plan (Integrated Report 2026), the land holding strategy is to reduce financial burden through option contracts, restrain spec starts and control inventory risk; DRB management methods (on-site decision authority, financial controls) are being rolled across the merged DRB/Brightland platform, and 'financing initiatives' are listed among the integration's efficiency measures. Division leaders own land decisions inside a central capital-allocation framework (HousingWire, May 2026). No DRB-specific owned/optioned target is published.

lots.note: DRB-level lots are not disclosed, so the fields are null. Parent figures: five pre-Tri Pointe U.S. builders (DRB incl. Brightland, Bloomfield, Edge, MainVue, Southern Impression) at 2026-09-30: 73,971 lots, 50,471 purchased, 23,500 under purchase contract (option) = 31.8% optioned; optioned lots -23.7% and owned -0.9% year on year (at 2025-09-30 the same group had 81,751 = 50,954 owned + 30,797 option, 37.7%). All six U.S. builders incl. Tri Pointe: 106,415 lots (67,154 owned, 39,261 option). At 2025-12-31: 79,565 lots (50,894 owned, 28,671 option, 36%). Our estimate: about 7 years of supply for the five-builder group (73,971 lots / 10,262 FY2025 units). DRB expected nearly 9,000 of the group's 2025 settlements (company release), so the five-builder numbers are dominated by DRB; this is an inference, not a disclosed DRB figure.

No seller, developer or land banker behind these contracts is named.
land_banking.note: Lot count is the five-builder group total, not DRB alone. Policy statement: Integrated Report 2026 (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/pdf/ar2026eng.pdf).

land_banking.description: Biscayne Homes' Tampa communities, acquired by DRB in March 2024, sit in master plans developed by Metro Development Group, so Metro is a lot source for DRB's Tampa operation. Terms (finished-lot takedowns or options) are not stated.
land_banking.source_title: DRB Group news: DRB Group Announces Acquisition of Tampa Homebuilder, Biscayne Homes (2024-03-01)
land_banking.note: Company release states the Metro master-plan location; that Metro supplies DRB lots on option terms is our inference. Source is older than 24 months with no newer confirmation. Verifier 2026-11-19: source URL corrected from /news/ to /news/post/ (old path redirected to the homepage); release confirms the Metro master-plan location. Sumitomo release https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20240329_01.pdf also says Biscayne had a strong relationship with Metro and a pipeline of numerous lots.

capital_events.description: Sumitomo Forestry America contributed its ownership of Brightland Homes, Ltd. (Texas; 2024 revenue USD 1,350.2M, total assets USD 1,470.4M, net assets USD 870.8M) to DRB Enterprises, LLC as an in-kind contribution, folding Brightland under DRB.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Reorganization and Registered Name Change of a Subsidiary (2025-03-28)

capital_events.description: Brightland Homes, Ltd. renamed DRB Group Texas, LLC (instead of the planned Brightland Homes, LLC) after a brand-strategy review, 100% owned by DRB Enterprises, LLC with Ronald S. Salameh as President & CEO; removed from the parent's list of major subsidiaries.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding Change of Registered Name and Status of a Subsidiary (2025-12-15)
capital_events.note: Any Texas land contracts, option agreements or liens will now sit in the name DRB Group Texas, LLC (formerly Brightland Homes, Ltd.).

capital_events.description: Parent level: Sumitomo Forestry signed a one-year bridge loan of up to JPY 835.1 billion with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation to buy Tri Pointe Homes and to cover an assumed refinancing of Tri Pointe debt.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Conclusion of a Loan Agreement with Financial Covenants (2026-05-07)

capital_events.description: Parent told analysts its credit rating could be downgraded if U.S. conditions persist; net D/E about 1.4x and equity ratio 29.2% at 2026-09-30; about JPY 260 billion of acquisition funding still to be refinanced, with U.S.-dollar borrowing under consideration; U.S. housing companies, including the existing builders, are reviewing staffing to cut costs.
capital_events.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry 3Q FY12/2026 results conference call Q&A (2026-11-05)
capital_events.note: Not a rating change: a management statement of downgrade risk. Ratings at the time: R&I A+ (Stable), JCR AA- (Stable).

capital_events.description: DRB announced two mortgage joint ventures launching January 2027: DRB Mortgage with Acrisure Mortgage (east) and DRB Home Loans with Alta Home Lending (west), led by Matthew Wolf, SVP of Financial Services.
capital_events.source_title: DRB Group news: DRB Group Announces Two New Mortgage Joint Ventures (2026-09-23)
capital_events.note: DRB's first in-house mortgage capability; contrast with the parent's 2026-11-05 remark that its U.S. builders will also use Tri Pointe's mortgage company.

joint_ventures.description: DRB Mortgage, a mortgage joint venture serving DRB's eastern markets, planned to launch January 2027.
joint_ventures.source_title: DRB Group news: DRB Group Announces Two New Mortgage Joint Ventures (2026-09-23)

joint_ventures.description: DRB Home Loans, a mortgage joint venture serving DRB's western markets (the former Brightland footprint), planned to launch January 2027.
joint_ventures.source_title: DRB Group news: DRB Group Announces Two New Mortgage Joint Ventures (2026-09-23)

joint_ventures.partner: Build-to-rent capital partners (31 ownership groups, incl. Pine Grove Communities and sister company Crescent Communities)
joint_ventures.description: DRB Group Development builds rental communities for investor owners, either as fee builder (general contractor) or by building on DRB's balance sheet and selling at certificate of occupancy; in 2023 it had 53 communities under construction, contract or in the pipeline and expected to build 5,722 BTR homes over several years.
joint_ventures.source_title: DRB Group news: DRB Group Celebrates Six Years of Successful Build-To-Rent Business (2023-11-06)
joint_ventures.note: Source is a 2023 company release (older than 24 months); HousingWire (2026-05-19) confirms DRB's build-for-rent and fee-build lines continue but gives no partner names. Third-party capital funds these projects, which is the closest public analogue to off-balance-sheet land and construction capital at DRB.

key_metrics.credit_ratings: DRB: none (unrated). Parent Sumitomo Forestry: R&I A+ Stable (issuer, 2026-05-15), JCR AA- Stable (2026-06-18), R&I a-1 short-term; hybrid bonds A- (R&I) / A (JCR).

ma.counterparty: Brightland Homes, Ltd. (now DRB Group Texas, LLC), contributed by Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc.
ma.description: Intra-group combination: Sumitomo Forestry moved its Dallas-based builder Brightland Homes (the former Gehan Homes) under DRB Enterprises, LLC by in-kind contribution. The combined DRB has 19 divisions in 14 states, about 1,500 employees and expected nearly 9,000 settlements in 2025; Ronny Salameh remains CEO.
ma.map_impact: DRB goes from an East Coast builder (10 states) to a national one, adding Texas, Arizona, Colorado, Tennessee and Jacksonville; Brightland is no longer a separate builder and its divisions now report into DRB. Brightland's former CEO John Winniford was listed as its representative in March 2025 but Salameh by December 2025. The Texas entity was renamed DRB Group Texas, LLC on 2025-12-15, and the Brightland brand is being replaced by DRB Homes.
ma.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Reorganization and Registered Name Change of a Subsidiary (2025-03-28)
ma.note: Footprint and employee figures from DRB's release (https://www.drbgroup.com/news/post/sumitomo-forestry-to-consolidate-brightland-homes-under-drb-group); renaming from https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20251215_Notice_Regarding_Change_of_Registered_Name_and_Status_of_a_Subsidiary.pdf.

ma.counterparty: Tri Pointe Homes, Inc. (acquired by DRB's parent, not by DRB)
ma.description: DRB's parent Sumitomo Forestry bought 100% of Tri Pointe Homes at USD 47.00 per share (about USD 4.0 billion for the shares), funded with an SMBC bridge loan. Tri Pointe becomes a second U.S. platform alongside DRB; the parent said it has no intention of merging everything at once.
ma.map_impact: DRB is no longer Sumitomo's only U.S. platform and now competes with a sister builder for parent capital: the Integrated Report 2026 footprint map shows states served by both, including Texas (DRB, Bloomfield and Tri Pointe). Group lots rise to 106,415 and the parent's leverage to about 1.4x net D/E, which tightens the capital DRB can draw and strengthens the case for off-balance-sheet lots. The parent also plans to have DRB and the other builders use Tri Pointe's mortgage company.
ma.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Notice Regarding the Completion of the Acquisition of Shares of Tri Pointe Homes (2026-05-14)
ma.note: Platform statements from the 2026-02-20 Q&A (https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20260220_Q%26A_from_the_Briefing_on_the_Acquisition_of_Shares.pdf); mortgage synergy from the 3Q Q&A (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/statements/pdf/2026_3q_qanda_en.pdf). Overlap from the Integrated Report 2026 map (https://sfc.jp/english/ir/library/pdf/ar2026eng.pdf); the map labels states by builder and only Texas is legible as a DRB + Tri Pointe overlap in the extracted text.

ma.description: Background, before the 2025 window: DRB bought the housing business of Tampa luxury builder Biscayne Homes, whose communities sit in Metro Development Group master plans. Builder Advisor Group advised the seller. Price not disclosed.
ma.map_impact: Gave DRB its Tampa and Southwest Florida division; Metro Development Group becomes a lot source in Tampa.
ma.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: US subsidiary DRB acquires housing business of Florida company (2024-03-29)

ma.counterparty: Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd. (through Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc.)
ma.description: Background: Sumitomo Forestry acquired DRB Group in 2016, its entry into six East Coast states including Maryland. It held 92.48% of DRB Enterprises, LLC via Sumitomo Forestry America at March 2025.
ma.map_impact: Explains why DRB has no public debt or filings: ownership and funding run through Sumitomo Forestry, and minority equity (7.52%) is held by others, presumably management, not named.
ma.source_title: Sumitomo Forestry: Acquisition of Shares of Tri Pointe Homes, investor presentation (2026-02-13), U.S. milestones slide
ma.note: Ownership % from https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20250331_01.pdf. Identity of the 7.52% minority holder(s) is not disclosed; 'presumably management' is our inference from the parent's stated practice of leaving founders with equity (2026-02-20 Q&A).

gaps: DRB-level lot counts (owned, optioned, years of supply): not publicly disclosed; only Sumitomo Forestry group totals are published.

Named land banker, lot-option financier or land-banking program at DRB: none found in DRB releases, Sumitomo Forestry disclosures or the press searched (searches on DRB/Brightland with land bank, lot option, Millrose, Domain Real Estate, Angelo Gordon returned nothing DRB-specific).

Link between DRB and Domain Real Estate Partners, Millrose Properties, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon: none found. Kennedy Lewis is Tri Pointe's (DRB's sister company's) land banker per press, not DRB's. Checks on Essential Housing, IHP Capital, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton and Forestar were limited; a June 2026 Walton finished-lot release in DRB's states (Houston, DFW, Wilmington NC) names no builder.

DRB credit facility, construction or land loans, agent bank and lender names: not publicly disclosed (private subsidiary, no SEC filings, no rated debt). State UCC lien searches on DRB entities (Maryland, Texas) were not run.
Size, rate and terms of Sumitomo Forestry shareholder loans to DRB: not publicly disclosed.
DRB cash, total debt, liquidity, revenue and closings: not publicly disclosed at DRB level (the only entity financials published are Brightland Homes, Ltd. for 2022-2024 in parent notices).
Identity of the 7.52% minority owners of DRB Enterprises, LLC: not publicly disclosed.

Unconfirmed claim: a Signalbase M&A page (trysignalbase.com, dated 2026-02-13, no source cited) says 'Chesmar Homes acquired DRB Group'. Not used: Sumitomo Forestry's 3Q FY12/2026 Factbook (2026-11-05) still lists DRB Group as its consolidated U.S. subsidiary, DRB's own September 2026 release shows no change of ownership, and Chesmar's site carries Sekisui House U.S. builder branding. Treat it as an error.
M&A by DRB in 2025-2026 beyond the Brightland combination: none found. Knight Homes (Atlanta, 2020) and Fielding Homes are older acquisitions mentioned in trade press and not sourced here.
Ownership splits and capital commitments of the Acrisure and Alta mortgage JVs, and current build-to-rent partner list: not publicly disclosed.
